message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"2.17","text":"For likewise the pairing connected with Elijah, though due to come, was willingly left behind until another time, having decided to take it up on another suitable occasion. Therefore the one “among those born of women” came first; then the one among the sons of men came second. By following this sequence, it was possible to understand whose Simon is—the one who, before me, was first to come to the Gentiles—and whose I am, I who have come after him and come upon him as light upon darkness, as knowledge upon ignorance, as healing upon disease. So then, just as the true prophet told us, a false gospel must first come from a certain deceiver, and only then, after the destruction of the holy place, must a true gospel be sent out secretly to set right the heresies that will arise. After these things, toward the end, the Antichrist must again come first, and then our Jesus, who is truly the Messiah, must appear; and after that, when eternal light has risen, everything belonging to darkness must disappear.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἡ πρὸς τὸν Ἠλίαν συζυγία","chosen":"the pairing connected with Elijah","rationale":"συζυγία denotes a conjunction or paired counterpart in the author’s sequence of paired figures; “connected with” leaves the precise relationship open."},{"source_quote":"ἄλλοτε εὐκαίρως αὐτὴν ἀπολαβεῖν","chosen":"to take it up on another suitable occasion","rationale":"The referent of αὐτήν is not explicit. “Take it up” reflects ἀπολαβεῖν while allowing the pairing or its deferred fulfillment to be intended; “receive it” or “recover it” are possible alternatives."},{"source_quote":"τίνος ἐστὶν Σίμων ... καὶ τίνος ὢν τυγχάνω","chosen":"whose Simon is ... and whose I am","rationale":"The repeated τίνος expresses affiliation or belonging within the paired sequence; specifying a particular owner, side, or spiritual source would resolve an ambiguity the Greek leaves open."},{"source_quote":"τὸν ὄντως χριστὸν ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦν","chosen":"our Jesus, who is truly the Messiah","rationale":"Χριστός functions as a title here, emphasized by ὄντως, rather than merely as part of a conventional personal name."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"2.18","text":"Since, then, as I said, some people are ignorant of the rule of pairing, for this reason they do not know who Simon, the one who went ahead of me, actually is. For if he were known, he would not have been believed. But now, because he is unknown, he has wrongly been believed. The one who does what haters do has been loved; the enemy has been welcomed as a friend; though he is death, he has been desired as one who saves; though he is fire, he has been regarded as light; and though he is a deceiver, he is listened to as one who speaks the truth. When I, Clement, heard these things, I said, “Who, then, is this man, such a great deceiver? I would like to know.” Peter said, “If you wish to learn, it is within your reach to find out from those from whom I too accurately learned everything concerning him.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὸν κανόνα τῆς συζυγίας","chosen":"the rule of pairing","rationale":"κανών is the governing pattern or rule, while συζυγία continues the author’s technical language of paired figures."},{"source_quote":"ὁ τὰ μισούντων ποιῶν","chosen":"the one who does what haters do","rationale":"The Greek literally refers to doing “the things of those who hate.” This rendering preserves that unusual expression; “the deeds of hatred” is a smoother but less formally exact alternative."},{"source_quote":"θάνατος ὢν ὡς σώζων πεπόθηται","chosen":"though he is death, he has been desired as one who saves","rationale":"The contrast identifies him with death and presents him as falsely desired in the role of a saving figure; “as a savior” would be an idiomatic alternative."},{"source_quote":"πάρεστίν σοι τὸ γνῶναι","chosen":"it is within your reach to find out","rationale":"The expression states that the opportunity or means of knowing is available to Clement, not merely that knowledge is physically present."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"2.19","text":"There is among us a certain Justa, a Syrophoenician and a Canaanite by ancestry, whose little daughter was afflicted by a severe disease. She approached our Lord, crying out and pleading that he heal her little daughter. But he, when appealed to by us as well, said, “It is not permitted to heal the Gentiles, who resemble dogs because they use different foods and practices, since what belongs at the royal table has been allotted to the sons of Israel.” When she heard this, wishing, like a dog, to share in crumbs falling from that same table, she changed what she had been by living in the same way as the sons of the kingdom, and obtained, as she had requested, healing for her little daughter. For had she remained a Gentile—being a Gentile and continuing in the same way of life—he would not have healed her, since in the first place it was not permitted to heal her as a Gentile.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"συρροφοινίκισσα, τὸ γένος χανανῖτις","chosen":"a Syrophoenician and a Canaanite by ancestry","rationale":"The first term identifies her regional or ethnic designation, while τὸ γένος explicitly marks Canaanite descent or ancestry."},{"source_quote":"τὸ θυγάτριον","chosen":"little daughter","rationale":"The diminutive form is retained as “little daughter.” It may be affectionate or lexicalized rather than a precise statement of age."},{"source_quote":"ὁ δὲ καὶ ὑφ’ ἡμῶν ἀξιωθεὶς","chosen":"But he, when appealed to by us as well","rationale":"In this context ἀξιωθείς describes his being petitioned or entreated by the disciples; the more literal “deemed worthy by us” would not fit the following response as naturally."},{"source_quote":"ἀποδεδομένης τῆς κατὰ τὴν βασίλειον τραπέζης","chosen":"since what belongs at the royal table has been allotted","rationale":"The printed construction has a case difficulty. The deliberately general “what belongs at” preserves the evident table imagery without silently supplying “food” or “portion”; either could be understood from the context."},{"source_quote":"μεταθεμένη ὅπερ ἦν, τῷ ὁμοίως διαιτᾶσθαι τοῖς τῆς βασιλείας υἱοῖς","chosen":"she changed what she had been by living in the same way as the sons of the kingdom","rationale":"The articular infinitive with the dative article expresses the means by which the change occurred. διαιτᾶσθαι concerns manner of life, including the foods and practices just mentioned."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"ἀποδεδομένης τῆς κατὰ τὴν βασίλειον τραπέζης","issue":"The genitive τραπέζης does not agree with the accusative phrase introduced by κατά, τὴν βασίλειον. The sense remains contextually recoverable, but the printed construction appears to contain a local case-form defect or an unusually compressed ellipsis.","proposed_reading":"ἀποδεδομένης τῆς κατὰ τὴν βασίλειον τράπεζαν","blocks_publication":false},{"source_quote":"τῆς βασιλείας .υἱοῖς","issue":"The printed full stop occurs inside the noun phrase and appears to be stray punctuation rather than a sentence boundary.","proposed_reading":"τῆς βασιλείας υἱοῖς","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"2.20","text":"This very woman, then, after adopting a way of life according to law, was driven from her own home, together with her healed daughter, by her own husband, who held opinions opposed to ours. But she, remaining faithful to her agreements and having abundant means, herself remained a widow, while she arranged her daughter’s marriage to a certain man who was favorably disposed toward the true faith and was poor. Then, being deprived also of her daughter because of the marriage, she bought two boys, educated them, and had them in place of sons. Having been educated together with Simon the magician from childhood, they learned thoroughly everything concerning him; for their friendship with him was so close that they even kept company with him in everything he wished to share with them.","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"νόμιμον ἀναδεξαμένη πολιτείαν","chosen":"after adopting a way of life according to law","rationale":"πολιτεία denotes a manner of life or conduct, and νόμιμον connects it with law-observant practice rather than merely describing it as socially respectable."},{"source_quote":"εὐγνωμονοῦσα πρὸς τὰς συνθήκας","chosen":"remaining faithful to her agreements","rationale":"The phrase describes honorable fidelity toward established agreements, probably her marital commitments in context; “marriage covenant” is possible but more specific than the Greek itself."},{"source_quote":"τῆς θυγατρὸς προφάσει γάμου στερηθεῖσα","chosen":"being deprived also of her daughter because of the marriage","rationale":"πρόφασις can indicate the occasion or stated reason, not necessarily a deceptive pretext. The sense is that the daughter’s marriage deprived Justa of her presence or companionship."},{"source_quote":"δύο παῖδας ὠνησαμένη","chosen":"she bought two boys","rationale":"ὠνησαμένη explicitly describes purchase, while the following statement that she treated them as sons supports taking παῖδας as boys rather than generically as children."},{"source_quote":"τοσαύτη γὰρ αὐτῶν ἦν ἡ φιλία, ὡς καὶ συνοστεῦσαι αὐτῷ","chosen":"their friendship with him was so close that they even kept company with him","rationale":"συνοστεῦσαι denotes close association or companionship. “Lived together with him” is possible but would make a more specific residential claim."},{"source_quote":"ἐν πᾶσιν οἷς βούλοιτο αὐτοῖς ἐνοῦν","chosen":"in everything he wished to share with them","rationale":"Taking ἐνοῦν as corresponding in sense to ἑνοῦν, “unite,” gives the idea of joining or sharing things with them. Another possible interpretation is “in everything in which he wished them to be present.”"}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"οἷς βούλοιτο αὐτοῖς ἐνοῦν","issue":"The smooth-breathed ἐνοῦν and its construction with οἷς and αὐτοῖς are unusual. It can be understood as a form corresponding to ἑνοῦν, “to unite,” supporting the sense “share with them,” while a conjectural change to αὐτοὺς ἐνεῖναι would yield “in which he wished them to be present.” The supplied reading therefore permits a defensible rendering but remains interpretively uncertain.","proposed_reading":"οἷς βούλοιτο αὐτοὺς ἐνεῖναι","blocks_publication":false}]}]}
